safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(والقلم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear"; (الواو) conjunction; (ما) an infinitival particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, with the referent pronoun omitted, i.e. what they write down, and the agent pronoun refers to the recording angels.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يسطرون) is in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to القلم.
The clause «(أقسم) بالقلم ...» has no grammatical position: initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «يسطرون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما).
2- (ما) negative, governing as ليس governs; (بنعمة) attached to the sense of negation in (ما), and (الباء) is causal [Note: I.e. your being mad is negated because of the favour of your Lord upon you. It is not valid to attach it to مجنون, lest it convey the negation of a madness that is a favour from Allah, and there is no madness in existence that is a favour.]; (مجنون) genitive in form, accusative in position, as khabar (predicate) of ما ...
The clause «ما أنت ... بمجنون» has no grammatical position: response to the oath. 3- (الواو) conjunction; (لك) attached to the khabar of إنّ; (اللام) for emphasis, in the place of the lām of the oath; (غير) a naʿt (adjective) of (أجرا), accusative.
The clause «إنّ لك لأجرا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the oath.
4- (الواو) the wāw of conjunction; (اللام) for emphasis, in the place of the lām of the oath, in substitution for the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (على خلق) attached to the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «إنّك لعلى خلق ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the oath.

* Rhetoric:
The device of verbal correspondence (al-munāsaba al-lafẓiyya): in His words «ن وَالْقَلَمِ وَما يَسْطُرُونَ» and what follows, up to His words «غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ». This device consists in bringing words that are balanced in measure.
Metaphor in particles: in His words «وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلى خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ».
على in its literal sense conveys elevation over something (istiʿlāʾ), which is not intended in the verse, since the Messenger, upon him be peace, does not rise above the tremendous character and mount it, as a man mounts the back of a horse, for example. Rather it is by way of figurative usage and metaphor; by it is meant the Messenger's, upon him be peace, firm possession of the tremendous character and noble traits.

* Benefits:
- Good character:
Jābir related that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah sent me to complete noble traits of character and to complete good deeds." From al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about righteousness and sin, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Righteousness is good character, and sin is what wavers in your chest and you dislike that people should come to know of it." From ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The believer, by his good character, attains the rank of one who fasts and stands in prayer." Abū Dāwūd narrated it.
From Abū l-Dardāʾ: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is nothing heavier in the scale of the believer on the Day of Resurrection than good character, and Allah the Exalted hates the obscene, foul-mouthed person." al-Tirmidhī narrated it
and said:
a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
From Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Among the most beloved of you to Allah and the nearest of you to me in seating on the Day of Resurrection are those of you best in character."
From Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I served the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for ten years, and by Allah he never once said "uff" to me, nor did he say about anything: why did you do such-and-such, or why did you not do such-and-such.
5- 6

safi-cedvel:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (بأيّكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (المفتون) [Note: With a muḍāf omitted, i.e. the trial of the one tried; or without omission if المفتون is a maṣdar.], and (أيّ) is an interrogative noun.
The clause «ستبصر ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if the command of Allah comes, you will see [Note: The command of Allah is the Day of Resurrection according to one view, or the victory of the believers in this world according to another view.].
The clause «يبصرون ...» is in the position of jussive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause ستبصر.
The clause «بأيّكم المفتون» is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of seeing, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by أيّ [Note: Visual seeing is suspended — with fatḥa on the lām — from governing, according to the correct view, by the evidence of: أما ترى أيّ برق هاهنا ("Do you not see what lightning is here") ... and تبصر means ترى.].

* Morphology:
(المفتون): passive participle of the triliteral (فتن). Its pattern is مفعول.
It may also be a maṣdar, like المعقول and الميسور.
7-

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(هو) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is (أعلم); (بمن) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أعلم); (عن سبيله) attached to (ضلّ); (الواو) conjunction; (بالمهتدين) attached to the second (أعلم).
The clause «إنّ ربّك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive, containing the sense of a causal explanation of what precedes it.
The clause «هو أعلم ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
The clause «ضلّ ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «هو أعلم» (the second) is in the position of nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause هو أعلم (the first).
8- 16

safi-cedvel:8-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (لا) a prohibitive, jussive-governing particle, and the verb was vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
The clause «لا تطع ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if the deniers have gone astray, then do not obey them.
9- 13 (لو) an infinitival particle; (الفاء) conjunction; (الواو) conjunction; (مهين، همّاز، مشّاء، منّاع، معتد، أثيم، عتّل، زنيم) adjectives qualifying (حلّاف), genitive like it; (بنميم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مشّاء); (للخير) attached to (منّاع) [Note: Or the lām is redundant (zāʾida), for strengthening, and (الخير) is genitive in form, accusative in position, as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of منّاع.]; (بعد) an accusative adverb, attached to (زنيم), and the reference in (ذلك) is to the aforementioned preceding attributes ...
The interpreted maṣdar (لو تدهن ...) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the verb ودّوا ...
The clause «ودّوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — or a causal explanation of the prohibition. The clause «تدهن ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (لو).
The clause «يدهنون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause تدهن.
The clause «لا تطع» (the second) is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تطع (the first).
14- 16 (أن) an infinitival particle; (عليه) attached to (تتلى); (آياتنا) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (أساطير) khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هي".
The interpreted maṣdar (أن كان ...) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the lām, i.e. because he is possessed of ..., attached to an omitted verb indicated by the coming condition with its protasis and apodosis, i.e. he denied the signs of Allah because he was ...
The clause «كان ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «تتلى عليه آياتنا ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «سنسمه ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(10) حلّاف: intensive form of the active participle of the triliteral حلف. Its pattern is فعّال, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and a doubled ʿayn with fatḥa.
(11) همّاز: intensive form of the active participle of the triliteral همز, of the class of ضرب: one who finds fault with others and backbites them, or one who strikes people with his hand. Its pattern is فعّال.
(مشّاء): intensive form of the active participle of the triliteral مشى. Its pattern is فعّال.
(نميم): it was said that it is a maṣdar like النميمة, and it was said that it is the plural of النميمة, or a collective noun (ism jamʿ) for it, from the verb نمّ, of the class of نصر or the class of ضرب ... In al-Miṣbāḥ: النميمة is a noun, and النميم also ... Its pattern is فعيل.
(13) عتّل: meaning coarse and harsh, and it was said: fierce in disputing; a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from the triliteral عتل, of the class of ضرب. Its pattern is فعلّ with two ḍammas and a doubled lām.
(زنيم): meaning one of doubtful descent, or a base person known for his baseness; a ṣifa mushabbaha, its pattern being فعيل in the sense of فاعل, i.e. one attached to the people like the زنمة of a camel or sheep, which is the piece of the ear that is cut and left hanging, to identify it.
(16) نسمه: it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, for it is the imperfect of the mithāl weak verb وسم; its fāʾ was deleted in the imperfect, for it is a mithāl weak verb with kasra on the ʿayn in the imperfect. Its pattern is نعله, with fatḥa on the nūn and kasra on the ʿayn.
(الخرطوم): a noun meaning the nose. Its pattern is فعلول with ḍamma then sukūn, like زنبور.

* Rhetoric:
Metonymy (al-kināya): in His words «سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ».
He expressed it so as a metonymy for the utmost humiliation, because a brand on the face is a disfigurement — so much so that he ﷺ forbade it in animals and cursed the one who does it — so how much more so on the most honoured place of it, which is the nose, because of its prominence. It has been said: beauty is in the nose; they made it the seat of honour and pride, and derived from it الأنفة (disdain). And in the word الخرطوم there is contempt, because it is used only of the elephant and the pig; so in expressing the nose by this name there is a reinforcement (tarshīḥ) of the humiliation indicated by branding on that particular organ. What is meant is: We will disgrace him in this world, and humiliate him to the utmost degree.
17- 33

safi-cedvel:17-33.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) an infinitival particle; (إذ) an adverb of past time, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (بلونا); (اللام) the lām of the oath; (يصرمنّها) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn, which was deleted because of the succession of identical letters; the (الواو), deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil (agent); (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; and (ها) is an object pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), referring to the garden, i.e. its fruit; (مصبحين) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يصرمنّ.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما بلونا ...) is in the position of genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is بلوناهم.
The clause «إنّا بلوناهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «بلوناهم ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «بلونا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «أقسموا ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يصرمنّها ...» has no grammatical position: response to the oath.
18- (الواو) parenthetical [Note: Or circumstantial (ḥāliyya).]; (لا) negative ...
The clause «لا يستثنون ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical [Note: Or it is in the position of nominative as khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هم" ... and the nominal clause is a ḥāl.].
19- (الفاء) conjunction; (عليها) attached to (طاف); (من ربّك) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of طائف; (الواو) circumstantial ...
The clause «طاف عليها طائف ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause أقسموا.
The clause «هم نائمون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
20- (الفاء) conjunction; (كالصريم) attached to an omitted khabar of أصبحت ...
The clause «أصبحت ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause طاف ...
21- 22 (الفاء) conjunction; (مصبحين) is like the first; (أن) an explicative particle (ḥarf tafsīr) [Note: Or an infinitival particle ... and the interpreted maṣdar (أن اغدوا ...) is in the position of genitive by an omitted bāʾ, attached to (تنادوا).]; (على حرثكم) attached to (اغدوا), in the sense of "come forward"; (كنتم) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
The clause «تنادوا ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause أصبحت.
The clause «اغدوا ...» has no grammatical position: explicative (tafsīriyya).
The clause «كنتم صارمين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes.
23- 24 (الفاء) conjunction; (الواو) circumstantial; (أن) like the first, with both possibilities; (لا) a prohibitive, jussive-governing particle; (يدخلنّها) an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of jussive; (اليوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يدخلنّها), and likewise (عليكم) ...
The clause «انطلقوا ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause تنادوا.
The clause «هم يتخافتون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «لا يدخلنّها ... مسكين» has no grammatical position: explicative.
25- (الواو) conjunction; (على حرد) attached to (قادرين), which is the khabar of the incomplete verb غدوا [Note: It may be a ḥāl of the third-person pronoun in غدوا if the verb is complete (tāmm), in the sense of "they went out in the early morning".] ...
The clause «غدوا ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause هم يتخافتون [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يتخافتون, after the circumstantial wāw, with قد implied.]. 26- 27 (رأوها) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, which was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (بل) for digression (iḍrāb) ...
The clause «رأوها ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «إنّا لضالّون ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «نحن محرومون» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the saying.
28- (الهمزة) for reproachful interrogation; (لكم) attached to (أقل); (لولا) a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ).
The clause «قال أوسطهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لم أقل ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech.
The clause «لولا تسبّحون» has no [grammatical] position: a resumption within the scope of the first saying [Note: The second object of speech is omitted, its implied form being: keep away from disobedience.].
29- (سبحان) a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, accusative.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «(نسبّح) سبحان ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, a supplication.
The clause «إنّا كنّا ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech.
The clause «كنّا ظالمين» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
30- 32 (الفاء) resumptive; (على بعض) attached to (أقبل); (يا) a particle of the vocative and of lamentation; (ويلنا) one addressed in the vocative (munādā), a muḍāf, lamented over, accusative; (أن) an infinitival and subjunctive-governing particle; (خيرا) a second mafʿūl bihi; (منها) attached to (خيرا); (إلى ربّنا) attached to (راغبون) by its being made to carry (taḍmīn) the meaning of راجعون "returning".
The clause «أقبل بعضهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يتلاومون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of بعضهم. The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, with قد implied.].
The clause «النداء والتحسّر» (the vocative and lamentation) has no grammatical position: parenthetical, a supplication.
The clause «إنّا كنّا ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech.
The clause «كنّا طاغين» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
The clause «عسى ربّنا ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «يبدلنا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبدلنا) is in the position of accusative as khabar of عسى.
The clause «إنّا ... راغبون» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
33- (كذلك) attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (العذاب); (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), for emphasis; (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle ...
The clause «كذلك العذاب ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «عذاب الآخرة أكبر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كانوا يعلمون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive ... and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "they would not have opposed Our command".
The clause «يعلمون ...» is in the position of accusative as khabar of كانوا ...

* Morphology:
(18) يستثنون: it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by making quiescent and iʿlāl by deletion. Its original form is يستثنيون — with a yāʾ with ḍamma before the wāw. The ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent and the vowel was transferred to the nūn — iʿlāl by making quiescent; when two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ was deleted — iʿlāl by deletion. Its pattern is يستفعون.
(19) طاف: it contains iʿlāl by substitution; its original form is طوف, its imperfect being يطوف; the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was changed into alif.
(نائمون): plural of نائم, active participle of the triliteral نام. Its pattern is فاعل, and the weak letter was changed into hamza by regular substitution.
(20) الصريم: a noun for the night of intense darkness, because of its being cut off (انصرام) from the day; or a noun for the orchard whose fruits have been cut, so it is فعيل in the sense of مفعول ... الصريم may also be applied to a large stretch of sand.
(22) اغدوا: it contains iʿlāl by deletion, beginning from the imperfect ... its original form in the imperfect is يغدوون — with a wāw with ḍamma after the dāl; then the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the dāl before it because of heaviness, and when two quiescent letters met, the wāw, the lām of the word, was deleted ... then the iʿlāl was carried over to the imperative اغدوا. Its pattern is افعوا.
(صارمين): plural of صارم, active participle of the triliteral صرم. Its pattern is فاعل.
(25) غدوا: it contains iʿlāl by deletion; the lām of the word was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Its pattern is فعوا.
(حرد): the maṣdar of the triliteral حرد meaning "to intend", of the class of ضرب. Its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn. It was said that its meaning is prevention, and it was said anger and rancour, and it may be of the class of فرح; and it was said it is withdrawing apart, of the class of نصر.
(32) راغبون: plural of راغب, active participle of the triliteral رغب. Its pattern is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
Switching to the imperfect: in His words «وَلا يَسْتَثْنُونَ».
I.e. not making exception. In switching to the imperfect there is a kind of expression and a drawing of attention to the place of their error. [Translator's note: the source has «نوع تعبير» "a kind of expression"; «تعيير» "reproach" may be intended. Translated as written.]
Simile (al-tashbīh): in His words «فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَالصَّرِيمِ».
It is likened to the orchard whose fruits have been cut, so that nothing remained in it. It was said: الصريم is the night, i.e. it became burnt, resembling the night in blackness. And it was said: like the morning, in that it became white like harvested crops.
Dependent metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tabaʿiyya): in His words «أَنِ اغْدُوا عَلى حَرْثِكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صارِمِينَ».
غدا عليه is said when one raids; so He has likened their going out early to cut the fruit to an army's going out early against something, because the sense of overpowering and seizing is present in it, namely cutting and severing; this is by way of dependent metaphor. The metaphor may also be considered representative (tamthīliyya).

* Benefits:
- The owners of the garden:
From Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The garden was an orchard in Yemen called «al-Ḍarawān», two parasangs short of Ṣanʿāʾ, which the people of the road would tread. It had been planted by people of prayer. It belonged to a man who died, and three sons of his inherited it. He used to leave for the poor — when they cut their palms — everything the sickle passed over, and he used to take from it a year's provision and give the rest in charity to the poor. When the father died and the three sons inherited it, they said: By Allah, the wealth is little and the dependants are many; this was done only when the wealth was much or the dependants few, but now there is no room for us to do as our father used to do. And they plotted among themselves to go early, before people woke, so as not to give the poor anything. [Translator's note: the source prints «قيل» ("it was said"); «قبل» ("before") is evidently intended and is translated.] So they set off whispering among themselves, so that no one would hear them, but they found that orchard had turned black and dry, so they blamed one another and regretted their deed.
34-

safi-cedvel:34-34.t:
* I'rab:
(للمتّقين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (جنّات); (عند) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to the omitted khabar.
The clause «إنّ للمتّقين ... جنّات» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
35-

safi-cedvel:35-35.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī) — and for reproach and rebuke; (الفاء) conjunction; (كالمجرمين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The clause «نجعل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.: are We unjust in judgement, so that We make the Muslims like the criminals?

* Rhetoric:
The inverted simile (al-tashbīh al-maqlūb): in His words «أَفَنَجْعَلُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ كَالْمُجْرِمِينَ».
The basis of the speech is: shall We make the criminals like the Muslims? But it was reversed, going along with their belief that they are better than the Muslims. If, however, the meaning is taken to be that the doers of good are not like the corrupters, nor the God-fearing like the wicked, nor the Muslims like the criminals, in evil state, then there is no reversal in the simile.

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ما; (كيف) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), whose governor is تحكمون ...
The clause «ما لكم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تحكمون» has no grammatical position: a badal (substitute) of the clause ما لكم [Note: If the pause is complete at (لكم), the clause is resumptive.].

safi-cedvel:37-38.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), in the sense of بل and the interrogative hamza conveying reproach and rebuke; (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (كتاب); (فيه) attached to (تدرسون); the second (لكم) is the khabar of إنّ; the second (فيه) is attached to the khabar of إنّ; (اللام) for emphasis; (ما) a relative in the position of accusative as the noun of إنّ; (تخيّرون) an imperfect verb from which one of the two tāʾs has been deleted, and from which the third-person referent pronoun has been deleted, i.e. تخيّرونه.
The clause «لكم كتاب ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تدرسون ...» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب [Note: The pronoun in (فيه) may refer to their judgement, understood from the previous question, not to the book; it is then attached to the preceding "being settled" (istiqrār) to which (لكم) is attached. On that view the clause تدرسون is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (فيه) ... or it is resumptive.].
The clause «إنّ لكم فيه لما ...» is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of studying [Note: It is a reported (maḥkiyya) clause, i.e. it is what is studied in the book. The hamza of (إنّ) was due to have fatḥa, but the emphatic lām in its scope made the hamza take kasra.].
The clause «تخيّرون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).

* Benefits:
- Some of what is hidden in the clause reported by "saying":
Among reported clauses there are some that may be hidden. Of these, in what is reported after "saying": (فَحَقَّ عَلَيْنا قَوْلُ رَبِّنا إِنَّا لَذائِقُونَ). The basis is "you will surely taste My punishment"; then it was switched to the first person, because they spoke of that about themselves, as al-Farazdaq said:
ألم تر أني يوم جوّ سويقة ... بكيت فنادتني هنيدة ماليا
(Did you not see that on the day of Jaww Suwayqa I wept, and Hunayda called to me: "What is the matter with me?")
The basis is: مالك ("what is the matter with you"). And of it, in what is reported after something containing the meaning of saying, is His words: (أَمْ لَكُمْ كِتابٌ فِيهِ تَدْرُسُونَ. إِنَّ لَكُمْ فِيهِ لَما تَخَيَّرُونَ), i.e. you study in it this wording, or you study in it Our saying this speech. That is either on the view that they were addressed with that in the book, according to their claim; or the basis is "they shall surely have what they choose", then it was switched to address when facing them. And it has been said about His words «يَدْعُوا لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ أَقْرَبُ مِنْ نَفْعِهِ» that يدعو is in the sense of يقول ("says"), like it in the words of ʿAntara:
يدعون عنتر والرماح كأنها ... أشطان بئر في لبان الأدهم
(They call "ʿAntar!" while the spears are like well-ropes in the breast of the black horse.)
— for whoever narrates it «عنتر» with ḍamma, as a vocative — and that (من) in the aforementioned verse is a mubtadaʾ, and (لبئس المولى) its khabar, and what is between them is a nominal clause as ṣila; and the clause of (من) with its khabar is reported by يدعو, i.e. the disbeliever says that on the Day of Resurrection. And it was said: من is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "is his god", and that this is a report of what he says in this world; on this view the basis is: he says "the idol is his god"; then the idol was expressed as "one whose harm is nearer than his benefit", to denounce the disbeliever.

safi-cedvel:39-39.t:
* I'rab:
(أم لكم أيمان) is like أم لكم كتاب «1»; (علينا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أيمان) [Note: Or attached to a naʿt (adjective) of أيمان.]; (إلى يوم) attached to the "being settled" (istiqrār) which is the khabar (predicate) [Note: Or attached to بالغة.]; (إنّ لكم لما تحكمون) is like إنّ لكم ... لما تخيّرون «4» ...
The clause «لكم أيمان ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive. The clause «إنّ لكم لما تحكمون ...» has no grammatical position: response to the oath understood from the context of the verse لكم علينا أيمان ...
The clause «تحكمون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(بالغة): feminine of بالغ, meaning firm and binding ... see verse (95) of Surat al-Māʾida,

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّهم) an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) ... and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi; (بذلك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (زعيم), the reference being to the judgement by which the disbelievers judge; (زعيم) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ أيّهم, nominative ...
The clause «سلهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أيّهم ... زعيم» is in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of asking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative أيّهم, and that with a preposition implied.

* Morphology:
(سلهم): its ʿayn — the hamza — has been deleted for lightness, optionally; and the deletion of the hamza in it entailed the deletion of the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) at its beginning. Its pattern is فلهم ... The hamza may be retained in this verb, and the connecting hamza restored, outside the verse ...

safi-cedvel:41-41.t:
* I'rab:
(أم لهم شركاء) is like أم لكم كتاب [Note: In verse (37) of the surah.]; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (اللام) the lām of command; (بشركاء) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يأتوا); (كانوا) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
The clause «لهم شركاء ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ليأتوا ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if they have partners, let them bring ... [Note: Or: if they are truthful in what they say ... and the mentioned clause إن كانوا صادقين is explicative.].
The clause «إن كانوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive ... and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes.

safi-cedvel:42-43.t:
* I'rab:
(يوم) an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يأتوا) [Note: Or it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember" ...]; (عن ساق) the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb يكشف; (الواو) in (يدعون) is the nāʾib fāʿil; (إلى السجود) attached to (يدعون); (الفاء) conjunction; (لا) negative ...
The clause «يكشف عن ساق ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يدعون ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause يكشف عن ساق.
The clause «لا يستطيعون ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause يدعون.
43- (خاشعة) an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (يدعون); (أبصارهم) the fāʿil (agent) of the active participle خاشعة, nominative; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (قد) a particle of realisation (ḥarf taḥqīq); (إلى السجود) attached to the second (يدعون); (الواو) circumstantial ...
The clause «ترهقهم ذلّة ...» is in the position of accusative as an emphasising ḥāl of the nāʾib fāʿil of يدعون.
The clause «قد كانوا ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl [Note: Or an emphasising resumption of the content of what preceded.].
The clause «يدعون» (the second) is in the position of accusative as khabar (predicate) of كانوا.
The clause «هم سالمون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in the second (يدعون).

* Morphology:
(سالمون): plural of سالم, active participle of the triliteral سلم, of the class of فرح. Its pattern is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
Representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in His words «يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ ساقٍ».
Uncovering it and tucking up from it is a proverbial image for the severity of a matter and the difficulty of an affair, because whoever falls into something that requires earnest effort tucks up [Translator's note: his garment] from his shin.
Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in His word «ساق».
ساق came indefinite to indicate that it is a matter indeterminate in its severity, unfamiliar, outside the ordinary.
The secret of attributing humility to the eyes: in His words «خاشِعَةً أَبْصارُهُمْ».
That is because its effect appears in them, for what is in the heart is known from the eye; so it is a rational (ʿaqlī) figure of speech.

safi-cedvel:44-45.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (الواو) conjunction; (من) a relative in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first-person pronoun in (ذرني); (بهذا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يكذّب); (الحديث) a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative, genitive — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it; (السين) for futurity; (حيث) an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to (نستدرجهم); (لا) negative.
The clause «ذرني ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if their states are thus, then leave Me ...
The clause «يكذّب ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «سنستدرجهم ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لا يعلمون ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
45- (الواو) conjunction; (لهم) attached to (أملي) ...
The clause «أملي لهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause سنستدرجهم.
The clause «إنّ كيدي متين» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya) ...

* Rhetoric:
Synecdoche / non-metaphorical figure (al-majāz al-mursal): in His words «وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ».
He called His granting them respite, and the succession of favours and bounties upon them, a "plot" because it is the cause of entanglement and destruction; for the reality of a plot is a kind of stratagem, because it is in its form: He, Glorified is He, does with them what is outwardly a benefit to them, while what He, Mighty and Majestic, intends by it is harm, because of what He knows of the vileness of their nature and their persistence in disbelief and ingratitude.

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), in the sense of بل and the hamza; (الفاء) causal (taʿlīliyya); (من مغرم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مثقلون) ...
The clause «تسألهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هم ... مثقلون» has no grammatical position: causal.

safi-cedvel:47-47.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) like the preceding one [Note: In the previous verse (46).]; (عندهم) an accusative adverb, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الغيب); (الفاء) conjunction.
The clause «عندهم الغيب ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هم يكتبون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يكتبون ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

safi-cedvel:48-50.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (لحكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اصبر) by its being made to carry (taḍmīn) the meaning of اخضع "submit"; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) a prohibitive, jussive-governing particle; (كصاحب) attached to the khabar (predicate) of تكن, with a muḍāf omitted [Note: I.e. let not your state be like the state of the companion of the fish.]; (إذ) an adverb in the position of accusative, attached to the implied muḍāf, i.e. like the state of the companion of the fish at the time of his calling out; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya).
The clause «اصبر ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if you fall into distress, then be patient ...
The clause «لا تكن ...» is in the position of jussive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause اصبر.
The clause «نادى ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «هو مكظوم» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
49- (لولا) a non-jussive conditional particle; (أن) an infinitival particle; (تداركه) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), from which one of the two tāʾs has been deleted [Note: Or it is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; the verb came masculine — which is permissible — because the fāʿil (agent) is figuratively feminine.], and (الهاء) is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من ربّه) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (نعمة); (اللام) linking the apodosis of لولا; (بالعراء) attached to (نبذ), and (الباء) is locative (li-l-ẓarf); (الواو) circumstantial.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تداركه ...) is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) ... and the khabar is omitted.
The clause «لولا (تدارك) نعمة ربّه ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «تداركه نعمة ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «نبذ ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «هو مذموم ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
50- (الفاء) conjunction in both places; (من الصالحين) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi.
The clause «اجتباه ربّه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لولا أن ...
The clause «جعله من الصالحين» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اجتباه.

* Morphology:
(48) مكظوم: passive participle of the triliteral كظم. Its pattern is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
Al-majāz al-mursal (non-metaphorical figure): in His words «وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ».
A majāz mursal, because blame (lawm) is in reality a cause of censure (dhamm); so the relation is causality.

safi-cedvel:51-52.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إن) lightened from the heavy one, necessarily left ungoverning (muhmala); (اللام) is the distinguishing lām (al-fāriqa); (بأبصارهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يزلقونك); (لمّا) an adverb in the sense of "when", containing the meaning of condition, in the position of accusative, attached to the implied apodosis; (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis [Translator's note: the source prints «للتوحيد» ("for unification"), evidently a misprint for «للتوكيد» ("for emphasis"), which is translated.] ...
The clause «يكاد الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive ...
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين). The clause «يزلقونك ...» is in the position of accusative as khabar (predicate) of يكاد. The clause «سمعوا ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. they almost made you slip.
The clause «يقولون ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause يزلقونك. The clause «إنّه لمجنون» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
52- (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (ما) negative, ungoverning (muhmala); (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (للعالمين) attached to (ذكر) [Note: Or attached to a naʿt (adjective) of ذكر.].
The clause «ما هو إلّا ذكر ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
